unverified.detail: Live v2 server rejects an explicit {"method":"subscribe","params":{"channel":"status"}} subscribe request with "Symbol(s) not found" (confirmed 2026-08-13, both via the real client core and a bare websocket connection) -- contradicts this endpoint's own notes, which derived the subscribe shape from the reconnection guide. The channel does auto-push a real status update immediately on connection with no subscribe at all, e.g. {"channel":"status","type":"update","data":[{"version":"2.0.10","system":"online","api_version":"v2","connection_id":15016751721099966496}]} -- but that arrives before/without any subscribe ack, so the real client's subscribe()-based surface cannot capture a passing example for it as currently spec'd.

spec.description: Subscribe to exchange status: automatically pushed once on successful connection and again whenever the trading engine status changes. There is no way to directly request a fresh status update.

channel.description: The channel this push belongs to.

type.description: This channel only ever pushes `update` -- there is no `snapshot` type.

data.description: One entry describing the current exchange status.

system.description: The status of the trading engine. `online`: markets operate normally. `maintenance`: markets are offline, no orders can be placed or cancelled. `cancel_only`: orders can be cancelled but not placed, no matching occurs. `post_only`: only `post_only` limit orders can be submitted, orders can be cancelled, no matching occurs. `limit_only`: documented separately on the WebSocket reconnection guide, not on this channel's own reference page.

api_version.description: The version of the WebSocket API.

connection_id.description: A unique connection identifier, for debugging.

version.description: The version of the WebSocket service.

notes: status.md documents no `Subscribe` request/response tab at all -- an apparent gap, since it is in fact a normal subscription: https://docs.kraken.com/exchange/guides/websockets/reconnection confirms `{"method": "subscribe", "params": {"channel": "status"}}` with no channel-specific parameters, so `requestBody` is omitted here (there is nothing beyond the implicit `channel` the `spec.channel` field already carries). No worked subscribe-ack example exists for this channel either; `StatusSubscribeResult` is inferred from the shared ack shape every sibling channel documents (`{channel, warnings}`, since `status` takes no `snapshot`/other param to echo), not from a directly observed example -- flagging in case a captured example later contradicts it. `system`'s enum is the union of two disagreeing sources: this channel's own page lists 4 values (`online`, `cancel_only`, `maintenance`, `post_only`); the reconnection guide's worked list adds a 5th, `limit_only`. Both are official docs.kraken.com pages; the union is kept rather than picking one, and the discrepancy is called out per rule 2/spec-authoring's 'documented is load-bearing' principle -- this is a same-day-fetched cross-page conflict, not a guess.

CAPTURE FINDING (2026-08-13): explicitly subscribing to `status` -- `{"method": "subscribe", "params": {"channel": "status"}}`, the exact shape this endpoint's notes derive from the reconnection guide -- is rejected by the live v2 server every time with `"Symbol(s) not found"`. Reproduced 3x, both through the real client core and via a bare `websockets` connection bypassing it entirely, so this is not a client bug. The channel does push a real, well-formed `status` "update" the instant the socket connects, with no subscribe needed at all -- so the assumption that `status` is "in fact a normal subscription" (this endpoint's existing note) does not hold against the real engine; it looks closer to a push-only, connection-triggered channel. Left `unverified` (`runtime_error`) instead of forcing a fake reply -- the next spec-authoring pass should decide whether `responses.reply` should be dropped/reworked for this endpoint, and how (or whether) the generated client should expose it at all.
